category_title: Adolescents who experience academic shut-down and loss of confidence during middle school transitions
minimal_context: Tony is working on a math homework assignment in his sixth-grade classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please take out your math homework and start working on the first section.

STUDENT: (Pushes the paper away) I don't see the point of this. It's just boring.

TUTOR: You need to complete the assignment. What do you think the first step is?

STUDENT: I don't know. I used to get Bs, but now in sixth grade everything is different.

TUTOR: Just read the instructions and do your best.

STUDENT: No, stuff started getting harder and I'm just quitting. I lost confidence a lot and it's all just failing anyway.

options.A: Persist relentlessly in checking on the student and getting to know him, regardless of the immediate results.
options.B: Compromise and negotiate situations by sharing decisions and power with the student instead of imposing control.
options.C: Provide instruction in math and other subjects using a modified curriculum for the student's daily assignments.
options.D: Provide flexibility with timelines by giving the student extra time to complete his math homework assignments.
